I farm here in Mwanza on my own land, growing mostly cassava and some sweet potatoes together with a bit of maize between the rows. Chemical fertilizer is too expensive for me and for root crops I don't really see the need — I put the manure from my goats and chickens on the plot instead, which has always worked for my family. I use the cuttings and vines I saved from last season's harvest because improved varieties are hard to find here and cost money I'd rather spend on my children's school. I rely on the rains, my wife and I do most of the work ourselves, and I only call a few neighbours to help when it's time to clear the land and harvest.
